strengths: R2E presents a coherent contribution to retrieval-based NLP: candidate entities are scored through retrieved, masked evidence, enabling passage-level attribution of the model output. Training with NULL evidence makes the Shapley intervention better motivated than arbitrary removal of inputs from an unprepared model.

The evaluation is substantial, including held-out literature, 60,839 gene-description facts, and 5,671 clinical therapeutic hypotheses. Gene-description performance improves meaningfully: uncorrected R2E achieves MRR 0.202 versus 0.176 for mean cosine similarity and 0.167 for MLM; frequency correction increases this to 0.260.

The clinical results support predictive competitiveness while providing evidence attributions. Literature-only R2E obtains AUROC 0.632 versus 0.630 for MLM and 0.545 for the genetics baseline. Incorporating additional evidence without retraining is demonstrated, and the genetics-only comparison provides useful evidence that learned semantic matching can improve over ontology-based matching.

The appendices provide extensive architecture, training, splitting, prompting, ablation, and runtime details. Training the literature models from scratch with temporal cutoffs is a valuable control. The three released evaluation datasets and candid examples of attribution and auditing failures are useful contributions.
weaknesses: Reproducibility remains a substantial obstacle to a clear Findings recommendation. The experiments depend on an unreleased corpus containing licensed full texts and a proprietary entity linker whose dictionaries and disambiguation model are insufficiently specified. Code and model weights are explicitly withheld. Detailed hyperparameters and public evaluation queries help, but do not provide an independently reproducible path to the reported results. A reproduction using an accessible corpus and specified preprocessing would materially strengthen the submission.

The explanation construction supports attribution to the selected evidence, but validation of explanation quality is limited. Clinical Shapley scores achieve only 0.665 AUROC against GPT-4 relevance labels. Human validation covers eight query–entity pairs per task with one expert per task; raw agreement of 71.5% and 82.2%, without label prevalence or inter-annotator reliability, is difficult to interpret. Agreement with GPT-4 does not establish agreement with experts. Direct expert evaluation and comparisons against retrieval similarity or simpler attribution methods are needed to substantiate the stronger reasoning-quality claims.

The clinical evaluation requires a narrower interpretation. The pre-2005 cutoff applies to literature, whereas no temporal cutoff is specified for the genetics data obtained from a 2024 resource; GPT-4 auditing also introduces later pretrained knowledge. Consequently, the combined and audited variants are not established as strictly prospective predictions. Moreover, filtering drugs by development date does not demonstrate that their gene–disease hypotheses were previously unvalidated. Discontinued development is also an imperfect proxy for lack of efficacy, as Appendix P acknowledges.

Some comparisons do not isolate the sources of improvement. Frequency correction substantially improves balanced ranking, but an equivalently corrected MLM baseline is not reported despite Appendix G describing that option. The uncorrected R2E improvements remain useful, but the larger corrected-model advantage is harder to attribute to the architecture. Likewise, the auditing gain from 0.633 to 0.638 lacks a control that selects evidence for the same auditing budget using retrieval similarity or random sampling.

Appendix F contains a mismatch with the stated negative-sampling procedure. Section 3.4 excludes the positive entity when sampling negatives, so the negative entity distribution is not independent of the query. Writing p = P(a|q,L=1) and N = |A|, the optimal logit is log((N−1)p/(1−p)), rather than log(Np). Ranking monotonicity is preserved, but the exact log-probability and PMI interpretations used to justify the correction require revision.
